headline: Bull agrees his plan has no proven edge: the desk gives it 36 wins in 100 when it needs 38, and every other version he tried also falls short, so skip.

messages.text: Final word from me. Bull was honest, and that honesty is my whole case: he says his plan 'does not pass' if the rules need a proven edge. The rules do, so I say skip.

messages.reply_to: Bull: a small, defined-risk dip-buy in an uptrend is acceptable
messages.text: Small size makes a bet cheaper, not better. The desk replayed his exact plan 10,000 times: the goal came first 36 times in 100 and the exit first 62 times. It needs 38 just to break even, and the average result is slightly negative.

He also tried four other shapes and every one landed under break-even. When every version you try loses a little, the problem is the trade, not the settings. The robot search found no good plan either.
A small fix to Bull's numbers: in real history, 13 times it reached the goal, 31 times it hit the exit first (and 15 neither). He said 33. It still points the same way.

Right now the price is 158.81, tucked under today's high of 158.85. The 1-hour chart is stretched (RSI 76.6, a 0 to 100 gauge where above 70 means 'run up a lot'), and the 5-minute and 15-minute momentum gauges have turned negative.

His entry, 158.76, is only 5 cents below the live price and sits right under an old ceiling at 158.768 where sellers have shown up before. His exit, 158.61, is just under another one at 158.66 that price already bounced off twice, and only about one normal hour's move away.

Also, the 10-year bond sale at 18:00 UTC is minutes away, and the hot-inflation news is hours old and already in the price. Wait for something better: a clean hold above 158.85, or a plan that pays more for the same risk.

argument:
Bull's strongest remaining point is that the risk is small and capped at 0.15, with the dollar index up 0.7%, 1h EMAs stacked up, event guard CLEAR and volatility normal. I accept those facts. They describe a trend that has already happened, though, not an edge on the next 8 hours. The desk replay of his final plan (entry 158.76, stop 158.61, target 159.00) gave 35.8% target-first, 62.5% stop-first and -0.047R on average against 38% needed at 1.6R gross; real history was 13 targets vs 31 stops of 59 (desk_r3.json, not 33 as Bull wrote). Lean: COIN_FLIP, and costs (spread, slippage) are not in that figure, so the net is worse than -0.047R. Optimizer is NO_EDGE (best 26.5% target-first, -0.099R).

Bull's four variants (his tm_*.json files) show the lack of edge is structural: 40.4% needs 44% at 1.26R, 33.9% needs 40% at 1.53R, 33.2% vs about 38% at 1.65R, 34.4% at 1.30R. A trade that misses break-even under every shape is not rescued by sizing. Limited downside is also not the same as positive expectancy.

Structure: the stop is 0.94x the 1h ATR (0.159), inside one normal hour; the desk flags it as stop_tight. Entry 158.76 sits just below the 158.768 swing high and the stop just under the 158.6615 level that turned price down twice. Momentum is fading short term (5m/15m MACD histograms -0.0071/-0.0041; 1h histogram 0.0855, down from 0.0896) with 1h RSI 76.6. A limit fill requires a dip, which is when the push is already failing (my reasoning, not a desk figure). The 18:00 UTC 10-year auction (Medium, tier 3) can move yields and the dollar, and context is only NEUTRAL.

Verdict: no measured edge, stretched price, tight stop, event risk minutes away. Skip.
